domain: planning law and land-use adjudication / regulatory appeal outcomes
prediction_question: For a planning-permission-family appeal (PINS casework type 'Planning Appeal' or 'Householder (HAS)') validated by the Planning Inspectorate, will the final decision be 'Allowed' rather than 'Dismissed', given only what is known at validation: casework type, LPA name and ONS code, LPA decision date, received date, procedure (written representations / hearing / inquiry), development type, appeal type reason and type-detail, site descriptors (area, floorspace, number of residences, green belt, agricultural holding, listed-building setting, conservation area, flooding issue, AONB, SSSI indicators), LPA application reference, and enforcement grounds where applicable?
prediction_time: 00:00 Europe/London on the appeal's Valid Date (the date PINS validated the case; present on 100% of the 186,785 measured decided rows). All outcome events (case start, allocation, hearing/inquiry, decision) postdate the instant; measured valid->decision lag is 91-365 days for 74% of cases. Every feature field is recorded from the appeal submission/registration and is documented by the publisher with a per-field data-quality grade (Appeals Data: Data notes and guidance). Post-instant fields are excluded by contract: Inspector Name (allocation after validation; publisher also warns apparent per-inspector outcome patterns are allocation artefacts), Start Date, Jurisdiction (mutable by recovery/derecovery), Date Recovered / Date Not Recovered / Call In Date, Redetermined, Bespoke, and the Decision/Decision Date columns themselves. Costs Applied for Indicator is treated as verify-at-construction (a costs application can be lodged after validation). This is a fixed RETROSPECTIVE benchmark over the current published files: the publisher revises the rolling database between editions ('data can change between different publications of this data set'), so historical operational as-of claims would need vintage evidence beyond this record (the update log documents monthly-to-quarterly publication since March 2018, so web-archive vintages are provable if a historical-availability claim is ever wanted).
target_definition: Binary from the publisher's Decision field (documented data quality 'Good'): positive = 'Allowed', negative = 'Dismissed'. Pre-specified eligibility rule: labelled population = s78_core casework types with Decision in {Allowed, Dismissed}; 'Split Decision' (1,350 5-yr / 1,440 older, all types) and 'Allowed in part' rows are excluded from the core task rather than coerced (recorded masses; a variant may map split->positive). Excluded outcomes (measured, all types): Unknown 3,186+1,969, No Decision Code Associated 148+72, Invalid 237+136, Turned Away 9+11, Appeal Withdrawn 243+169, missing 178+600. Enforcement/RoW/TPO/high-hedges casework uses a different outcome vocabulary (Notice upheld / varied and upheld / quashed) and is out of scope. Censoring is stated: the database contains DECIDED cases only (publisher: in-progress, withdrawn and turned-away cases are not included), so the population is outcome-conditioned by construction; the task is 'among validated appeals that reach a PINS decision, which succeed', not 'among all validated appeals'. Decision and Decision Date columns are excluded from shipped features.

license_evidence: Read 2026-10-31 from https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/planning-inspectorate-appeals-database/appeals-data-data-notes-and-guidance: 'This publication is licensed under the terms of the Open Government Licence v3.0 except where otherwise stated.'

Publication page (read 2026-10-31) carries the Open Government Licence emblem and 'Crown copyright 2026'; no dataset-specific restriction is stated on the publication page or the data notes - the publisher's own caveats are about attribution of outcomes to decision makers, not redistribution.

Publisher caveats to carry onto any release (data notes + publication page, read 2026-10-31): 'Some categorisation of appeals can be subjective'; 'data can change between different publications of this data set'; decided cases only (in progress / withdrawn / turned away not included); Local Plans Examinations rows removed from the current Casework Database; TPO valid dates removed by the publisher after a data-entry issue (TPO is out of the core task's scope); inspector-name data errors corrected 2025 (field excluded from features anyway); 'The Planning Inspectorate will not entertain a challenge to the appointment of any Decision Maker on the basis of this data.'
split_strategy: Temporal by decision year, counts computed from the source (probe_count.py, 2026-10-31 files, s78_core = Planning Appeal + Householder (HAS)): train 2016-2020 (older file) 65,483 rows, 19,577 allowed (29.9%); eval 2021-2022 (complementary halves of 2021 from both files: 10,199+3,442) 27,179 rows, 8,044 allowed (29.6%); holdout 2023-2026 (5-yr file, 2026 through October) 52,471 rows, 16,273 allowed (31.0%). Both classes present in every one of the 11 decision years (yearly allow rate 27.0%-34.6%, no drift). Positives are independent appeal events; the main clustering is by LPA (376-379 distinct) and by linked cases (Link Status/Lead Case present, 0 duplicate case numbers within each file) - an LPA-clustered bootstrap interval is planned for the reference comparison. Cross-file dedup must key on the composite (Type of Casework, LPA Name, Received/Valid/Decision dates, Decision) because the Older Casework Data reference numbers are explicitly NOT linkable to Casework Database case numbers (publisher-documented).

probe_2026_10_31.command: probe_count.py on both xlsx (stdlib zipfile+iterparse; full JSON at candidates/pins-planning-appeal-outcome/probe_results_2026-10-31.json)
probe_2026_10_31.cross_check_publisher_summary: PINS Annual Report 2022-23: 'In the last year three out of every ten appeals were allowed' - measured s78_core allow rate 29.0% (Planning Appeal) / 34.3% (Householder) in the 5-yr file, 29.9%/32.4% older; measured per-year s78_core allow rate 27.0%-34.6%, consistent with the publisher's published ~30% figure and stable across 11 years.

measurements.extraction_cost: Measured 2026-10-31 on the coordinator (4 vCPU, 1.9 GiB class): 2 anonymous HTTP GETs, 34,532,981 bytes total (22,207,115 + 12,325,866), 0.63 s + 0.58 s download wall clock; stdlib streaming parse of both files 26-33 s. Construction is worker-trivial: the complete source is 34.5 MB. sha256 recorded per file in sources.

next_action: GO to construction (advancement session owns it). Construction step: on a worker, re-download both Excel files by exact recorded URL (sha256-pinned), parse with pandas, restrict to s78_core, apply the pre-specified eligibility rule, dedup across files on the date composite, drop post-instant and PII columns (Inspector Name, Start Date, Jurisdiction, recovery/call-in/redetermined/bespoke, Appellant, Agent, Site Address, Data Source), engineer LPA-level prior-outcome features strictly from decision dates earlier than each row's validation instant, write train/eval/holdout CSVs, then full-worker qualification -> exact-byte acceptance -> reference/model scoring -> reporting in that order. Expected artifact: ~130-145k rows x ~25 columns, ~25-40 MB of CSVs (worker-trivial: the whole source is 34.5 MB). Decisive checks: qualification gate pass on the full artifact; measured paired model-vs-baseline AUC intervals on eval (baselines: LPA historical allow rate, procedure/casework-type base rates, calendar-only); go/no-go on demonstrated headroom over the LPA-prior reference, so a persistence-style win does not ship as a headline.

prior_art: PlanSureAI appeals search (plansureai.com/appeals; descriptive overturn rates only); APE Autonomous Research, 'The Inspector Lottery That Isn't: Small-Sample Bias in Examiner Leniency Designs Applied to England's Planning Appeals', ape.socialcatalystlab.org, 2026-04-09; PMC8392781 and PMC10683341 (PINS hot-food-takeaway appeal analyses, 2021/2023).
novelty_check.theirs: The publisher (PINS) ships the raw bulk Excel files plus descriptive quarterly '% allowed' statistics; PlanSureAI ships commercial appeal-decision search and LPA overturn-rate analytics over the same open data (199,531 decisions, no prediction benchmark, no splits); APE 2026 'The Inspector Lottery That Isn't' is an econometric examiner-leniency study on 2,227 scraped appeals (no ML-ready release); public-health thematic studies analyze small subsets (52-54 hot-food-takeaway appeals).
novelty_check.ours: A scored, temporally-split binary prediction task over the full official PINS Casework bulk panel (both GOV.UK Excel files, 11 decision years 2016-2026, ~187k decided cases, ~145k in the planning-permission family), with a submission-time feature contract that excludes post-instant fields (Inspector Name, recovery/call-in dates, Redetermined) and a documented eligibility rule for Split/Unknown decisions; shipped as train/eval/holdout with a reproducible construction script.
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
